heading_path: Accessibility
summary: What Won Toasts does for screen readers, keyboard users and motion sensitivity — and why none of it is behind Pro.
text:
Accessibility is **quality, not scope**, so every plan gets all of it. Pro never
unlocks an accessibility feature and Free never ships a degraded one.

heading_path: Accessibility › Screen readers
summary: What Won Toasts does for screen readers, keyboard users and motion sensitivity — and why none of it is behind Pro.
text:
Toasts render into an `aria-live` region so a screen reader announces them without
stealing focus. Routine confirmations announce politely; genuinely urgent messages
use the assertive role. The region is a status region, not a dialog — a shopper is
never trapped in it.

heading_path: Accessibility › Motion
summary: What Won Toasts does for screen readers, keyboard users and motion sensitivity — and why none of it is behind Pro.
text:
If the shopper's system asks for reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion`), entry
animations are dropped and the toast simply appears. Whatever animation you chose
in the design studio is overridden — the shopper's setting wins.

heading_path: Accessibility › Colour scheme
summary: What Won Toasts does for screen readers, keyboard users and motion sensitivity — and why none of it is behind Pro.
text:
The `system` theme mode follows the shopper's `prefers-color-scheme`, so a toast
does not flash a white card at someone browsing in dark mode.

heading_path: Accessibility › Pointer and touch
summary: What Won Toasts does for screen readers, keyboard users and motion sensitivity — and why none of it is behind Pro.
text:
The close (×) button meets the minimum touch-target size on mobile — this is
verified by a geometry test in the release gate, not just by eye.

heading_path: Accessibility › Time to read
summary: What Won Toasts does for screen readers, keyboard users and motion sensitivity — and why none of it is behind Pro.
text:
Auto-dismiss can be paused on hover, and a toast can be closed manually. If your
messages are long, raise the duration rather than relying on the shopper reading
fast; the setting lives under **Design → Timing & interaction**.

Related: [performance-and-compatibility](performance-and-compatibility),
[appearance-and-branding](appearance-and-branding).

doc_title: Anti-spam and how often toasts appear
heading_path: Anti-spam and how often toasts appear
summary: How Won Toasts prevents flooding a shopper — merge, caps, cooldowns and quiet mode — and which parts are Free versus Pro.
text: Found in the admin under **Design → Anti-spam**. Three layers, applied in order.

doc_title: Anti-spam and how often toasts appear
heading_path: Anti-spam and how often toasts appear › 1. Merge — several changes become one toast
section: 1. Merge — several changes become one toast
summary: How Won Toasts prevents flooding a shopper — merge, caps, cooldowns and quiet mode — and which parts are Free versus Pro.
text:
Rapid changes collapse into a single toast instead of a stack. You control what
counts as "the same thing" (**Group by**), how wide the merge window is
(**Merge changes within**), and whether quantity changes fold into one `+N`
(**Merge quantity changes into one "+N"**).

Note that adding the same product three times fast already produces **one** toast
with `+3` — that is the cart diff, not merging. Merging is for *different*
products or event types arriving together. See
[grouping-and-conflicts](grouping-and-conflicts).

doc_title: Anti-spam and how often toasts appear
heading_path: Anti-spam and how often toasts appear › 2. Cap — how much is too much
section: 2. Cap — how much is too much
summary: How Won Toasts prevents flooding a shopper — merge, caps, cooldowns and quiet mode — and which parts are Free versus Pro.
text:
- **Max toasts per session** — the hard ceiling per shopper visit.
- **Wait between repeats** — a cooldown before the same rule may fire again.
- **Hide a dismissed toast for** — if a shopper closes something, it stays gone.
- **Advanced (Pro):** max toasts per minute, and ignoring duplicates within a window.

**Free is capped too.** Free is held to a fixed per-session ceiling it cannot
raise (see [reference/plan-limits](../reference/plan-limits.generated.md) for the
number). Pro does not buy "protection" — protection is quality and every plan gets
it. Pro buys **control of the number**, including raising it or setting `0` for
unlimited.

doc_title: Anti-spam and how often toasts appear
heading_path: Anti-spam and how often toasts appear › 3. Quiet — mute everything
summary: How Won Toasts prevents flooding a shopper — merge, caps, cooldowns and quiet mode — and which parts are Free versus Pro.
text:
**Quiet mode** silences every toast until it expires. Use it during a migration,
a theme edit or a campaign you don't want commented on.

doc_title: Anti-spam and how often toasts appear
heading_path: Anti-spam and how often toasts appear › What this means when you debug
section: What this means when you debug
summary: How Won Toasts prevents flooding a shopper — merge, caps, cooldowns and quiet mode — and which parts are Free versus Pro.
text:
A toast that "should" have fired and didn't is usually governed, not broken. The
order of suppression reasons the engine records is: quiet mode → session cap →
cooldown → suppressed after dismiss. See
[troubleshooting](../support/troubleshooting).

Related: [grouping-and-conflicts](grouping-and-conflicts),
[notifications-and-recipes](notifications-and-recipes).

heading_path: Appearance and branding › The default look (all plans)
summary: What can be styled (light/dark by default, full design studio on Pro) and when the "Powered by Won" badge shows.
text:
Out of the box, toasts follow a clean neutral design that adapts to **light / dark
/ system** (it respects the shopper's `prefers-color-scheme`) and honors
`prefers-reduced-motion`. This default is fully usable and accessible on the Free
plan — appearance is **scope**, not a quality gate.

heading_path: Appearance and branding › Design studio (Pro)
summary: What can be styled (light/dark by default, full design studio on Pro) and when the "Powered by Won" badge shows.
text:
On Pro, the **Appearance** admin page unlocks the design studio:

- Theme mode and custom colors
- Per-event accent color
- Radius, width, shadow, density
- Animation style (slide / fade / pop / slide-scale)
- Icon set

Accepted values are in
[reference/config-options](../reference/config-options.generated.md). A **live
preview** in the admin renders with the *same* engine as the storefront, so what
you see is what shoppers get.

heading_path: Appearance and branding › Rendering isolation
summary: What can be styled (light/dark by default, full design studio on Pro) and when the "Powered by Won" badge shows.
text:
Toasts render inside a **Shadow DOM** with their own stylesheet and CSS custom
properties, so the theme's CSS can't bleed in and the toasts can't disturb the
theme. This is why they look consistent across themes (Dawn, Horizon, …).

heading_path: Appearance and branding › "Powered by Won" badge
summary: What can be styled (light/dark by default, full design studio on Pro) and when the "Powered by Won" badge shows.
text:
The Free plan shows a small **"Powered by Won"** badge on toasts. Removing it is a
Pro feature (`remove_branding`). See
[reference/plan-limits](../reference/plan-limits.generated.md).

Related: [plans-free-vs-pro](plans-free-vs-pro), task:
[customize-appearance](../tasks/customize-appearance.md).

doc_title: Cart toasts and how they trigger
heading_path: Cart toasts and how they trigger
summary: How cart toasts detect add/remove/change events, show the quantity delta, and offer Undo on removals.
text: A **cart toast** is the notification shown when the shopper's cart changes.

doc_title: Cart toasts and how they trigger
heading_path: Cart toasts and how they trigger › How a change is detected
summary: How cart toasts detect add/remove/change events, show the quantity delta, and offer Undo on removals.
text:
Won Toasts watches storefront cart requests (`/cart/add`, `/cart/change`,
`/cart/update`, `/cart/clear`) and the theme's `cart:updated` event, then
reconciles against the real cart (`/cart.js`). It shows the **net change**, so
three quick adds of the same product become **one** toast reading `+3`, not three
separate ones.

Each toast derives from a cart event of one of these kinds: item **added**,
**removed**, **increased**, or **decreased**. The exact machine-readable list is
in [reference/event-types](../reference/event-types.generated.md).

doc_title: Cart toasts and how they trigger
heading_path: Cart toasts and how they trigger › What a toast contains
summary: How cart toasts detect add/remove/change events, show the quantity delta, and offer Undo on removals.
text:
- Product image and name
- The quantity change (delta, e.g. `+2` / `−1`)
- A colored accent that depends on the event type
- On **removals**: an **Undo** action

doc_title: Cart toasts and how they trigger
heading_path: Cart toasts and how they trigger › Undo
summary: How cart toasts detect add/remove/change events, show the quantity delta, and offer Undo on removals.
text:
Undo is the **only** cart write the app performs on its own, and only when the
shopper clicks it — it re-adds the removed item. Everything else is read-only
observation of the cart.

doc_title: Cart toasts and how they trigger
heading_path: Cart toasts and how they trigger › What it does not do
summary: How cart toasts detect add/remove/change events, show the quantity delta, and offer Undo on removals.
text:
- It does not create a second product form or change add-to-cart behavior.
- It does not modify prices.
- It ignores gift lines (`_gift_progress`) so a system-added free gift does not
  fire a normal "item added" toast — those are handled as
  [milestones](milestones).

Related: [grouping-and-conflicts](grouping-and-conflicts),
[appearance-and-branding](appearance-and-branding).

heading_path: Grouping, anti-spam and conflicts
summary: How Won Toasts avoids toast spam by grouping bursts, deduping, rate-limiting, and summarizing multiple milestones.
text: Won Toasts keeps notifications calm even when a lot happens at once.

heading_path: Grouping, anti-spam and conflicts › Net change, not per-click
summary: How Won Toasts avoids toast spam by grouping bursts, deduping, rate-limiting, and summarizing multiple milestones.
text:
Repeated changes to the **same product** collapse into their net result before a
toast is ever shown — three quick adds become one `+3` toast. This happens at the
cart-reconcile level, so it's automatic.

heading_path: Grouping, anti-spam and conflicts › Grouping across different products
summary: How Won Toasts avoids toast spam by grouping bursts, deduping, rate-limiting, and summarizing multiple milestones.
text:
When several **different** products or types change in one burst, grouping decides
how they combine:

- **off** — one toast per change
- **by-product** / **by-variant** — merge changes to the same product/variant
- **by-type** — merge by event type (all "added" together, etc.)

Merged toasts sum their deltas. The accepted values are in
[reference/config-options](../reference/config-options.generated.md).

heading_path: Grouping, anti-spam and conflicts › Anti-spam guardrails
summary: How Won Toasts avoids toast spam by grouping bursts, deduping, rate-limiting, and summarizing multiple milestones.
text:
- **Dedupe window** — suppresses an identical toast fired again within a short window.
- **Rate limit** — caps how many toasts appear per minute (a sliding 60s window).
- **Overflow** — when more toasts arrive than the max-visible limit, they either
  **queue** or **collapse** into a "+N more" chip.

heading_path: Grouping, anti-spam and conflicts › Conflicts and summaries
summary: How Won Toasts avoids toast spam by grouping bursts, deduping, rate-limiting, and summarizing multiple milestones.
text:
When multiple things qualify at the same time, toasts are ordered by **severity**
(warning → reward → success → info) and priority. If **two or more reward
milestones** fire together, they collapse into a **single summary toast** instead
of stacking — so the shopper sees one clear message, not a pile.

Related: [cart-toasts](cart-toasts), [milestones](milestones).

heading_path: Insights, holdouts and ROI
summary: What the Insights page measures, why proving revenue needs a holdout, and why the app refuses to show numbers it cannot stand behind.
text: **Insights** (Pro) is the admin's Reach + ROI page.

heading_path: Insights, holdouts and ROI › What is measured
summary: What the Insights page measures, why proving revenue needs a holdout, and why the app refuses to show numbers it cannot stand behind.
text:
- **Reach** — impressions and interactions, per toast type.
- **Most shown** — which toast dominates a shopper's session.
- **What we noticed** — plain-language diagnoses, each linking to the setting
  that would act on it.

Events are counted per day, per toast type, and are **scrubbed before storage**:
only a whitelist of typed fields survives, everything else — including anything
that could carry personal data — is dropped at the gate. See
[privacy-and-data](privacy-and-data).

heading_path: Insights, holdouts and ROI › Why some numbers say "needs holdout"
summary: What the Insights page measures, why proving revenue needs a holdout, and why the app refuses to show numbers it cannot stand behind.
text:
Order value and progression are shown as **"needs holdout"** until you turn one
on. Without a holdout group, "revenue after installing the app" is a correlation,
not a result — seasonality, traffic and campaigns all move it.

A **holdout** keeps a slice of shoppers toast-free, so the two groups differ only
in whether they saw a toast. **Monthly ROI** is only labelled *holdout-proven*
when that comparison actually exists.

heading_path: Insights, holdouts and ROI › Honest cold start
summary: What the Insights page measures, why proving revenue needs a holdout, and why the app refuses to show numbers it cannot stand behind.
text:
A store with no traffic gets "No toasts shown yet", not a zero-filled dashboard.
An aggregate below a credible sample size renders nothing at all. The same
principle as [notifications-and-recipes](notifications-and-recipes): silence
beats a number the app cannot stand behind.

heading_path: Insights, holdouts and ROI › A/B variants
summary: What the Insights page measures, why proving revenue needs a holdout, and why the app refuses to show numbers it cannot stand behind.
text:
An announcement can carry several variants (one per line); shoppers are split
evenly and the split is deterministic per shopper, so nobody sees a message
change mid-visit.

Related: [plans-free-vs-pro](plans-free-vs-pro), [privacy-and-data](privacy-and-data).

heading_path: Languages, translations and currencies
summary: How Won Toasts picks a shopper's language, how you translate messages, and why free-shipping thresholds are set per currency.
text:
The admin **Markets** page holds three things: your languages, the translations
of every message, and per-currency thresholds.

heading_path: Languages, translations and currencies › Languages come from your store
summary: How Won Toasts picks a shopper's language, how you translate messages, and why free-shipping thresholds are set per currency.
text:
Won Toasts does not ship a fixed language list. It reads the languages your
Shopify store actually publishes, and you can add extra BCP-47 codes by hand
(`pt-pt`, `sv`, `da`). One of them is the **default (fallback) language**.

How a shopper's message is chosen: exact locale (`pt-BR`) → the language
(`pt`) → your default language → English. A shopper never sees an empty toast
because a translation is missing.

Free stores get a small number of languages, Pro many more — exact limits in
[reference/plan-limits](../reference/plan-limits.generated.md).

heading_path: Languages, translations and currencies › Translations
summary: How Won Toasts picks a shopper's language, how you translate messages, and why free-shipping thresholds are set per currency.
text:
Every message template is editable per language, per toast type, in one matrix.
Placeholders (product name, quantity, remaining amount) stay identical across
languages — the app fills them in, including correct plural forms for languages
that need more than "one / other" (Czech and Slovak among them).

heading_path: Languages, translations and currencies › Currencies: one threshold per currency, not one converted number
section: Currencies: one threshold per currency, not one converted number
summary: How Won Toasts picks a shopper's language, how you translate messages, and why free-shipping thresholds are set per currency.
text:
A free-shipping milestone is **not** stored as a single amount that gets
converted. Each presentment currency gets its own threshold, edited under
**Markets → Currencies**. The base amount and the on/off switch stay with the
milestone itself on the **Toasts** page.

**Why:** a converted threshold drifts with the exchange rate, so the bar a shopper
sees would not match the shipping rate you configured in Shopify. Setting the
number per currency keeps the promise and the actual rate in sync.

Free stores keep a limited number of per-currency thresholds; the ones kept are
chosen alphabetically by ISO code so the same two survive on every request and the
shopper's progress bar never flickers.

Related: [milestones](milestones), [plans-free-vs-pro](plans-free-vs-pro).

heading_path: Milestones (free shipping and free gift)
summary: Milestones show progress toward a reward (free shipping, free gift); the app announces progress but does not grant the reward.
text:
A **milestone** is a reward the shopper is working toward — most commonly **free
shipping** at a cart subtotal, or a **free gift**. Won Toasts shows progress and
celebrates crossing the threshold.

heading_path: Milestones (free shipping and free gift) › How progress is tracked
summary: Milestones show progress toward a reward (free shipping, free gift); the app announces progress but does not grant the reward.
text:
As the cart changes, each milestone moves through a small set of states:

- **unreached** — below the threshold
- **approaching** — close to it
- **just_reached** — crossed it on this change (fires the celebration once)
- **reached** — still met
- **just_lost** — dropped back below (resets, so it can celebrate again later)

A milestone is celebrated **once** per cart, tracked per cart token, and re-armed
if the shopper falls back below the threshold.

heading_path: Milestones (free shipping and free gift) › Free shipping
summary: Milestones show progress toward a reward (free shipping, free gift); the app announces progress but does not grant the reward.
text:
Configured with a subtotal **threshold**. The toast shows the remaining amount
("$12 away from free shipping") and celebrates at the threshold. The subtotal used
is the eligible cart subtotal.

heading_path: Milestones (free shipping and free gift) › Free gift / Gift Ladder
summary: Milestones show progress toward a reward (free shipping, free gift); the app announces progress but does not grant the reward.
text:
Won Toasts detects a **gift line** on the cart (the `_gift_progress` line-item
convention) and treats reaching it as a gift milestone. This integrates with a
Gift Ladder setup **without requiring** any specific other app — it only reads the
line convention.

heading_path: Milestones (free shipping and free gift) › Announce, don't grant
summary: Milestones show progress toward a reward (free shipping, free gift); the app announces progress but does not grant the reward.
text:
Milestones **announce** progress. The actual free shipping or gift is delivered by
your **Shopify shipping rules / discounts / gift automation** — Won Toasts never
grants a reward or changes a price. If a toast says "free shipping unlocked" but
shipping still costs money at checkout, the Shopify shipping rule is the thing to
check, not the app.

Related: [cart-toasts](cart-toasts), [grouping-and-conflicts](grouping-and-conflicts),
task: [set-up-free-shipping-milestone](../tasks/set-up-free-shipping-milestone.md).

heading_path: Notifications (recipes) beyond the cart
summary: Recipes are merchant-configured toasts that fire on page views rather than on the shopper's own cart — countdown, announcement, low stock and cart activity.
text:
[Cart toasts](cart-toasts) react to what *this* shopper just did. **Recipes** —
listed on the **Toasts** page in the admin — are rules you switch on yourself, and
they can fire on a page view instead of a cart change.

heading_path: Notifications (recipes) beyond the cart › The recipes
summary: Recipes are merchant-configured toasts that fire on page views rather than on the shopper's own cart — countdown, announcement, low stock and cart activity.
text:
| Recipe | What the shopper sees | Plan |
|---|---|---|
| **Cart toasts** | Every add, remove and quantity change confirmed | Free |
| **Countdown timer** | A real deadline ticking down | Free |
| **Announcement** | Your own message — a sale, a shipping cutoff | Free |
| **Low-stock urgency** | "Only 3 left" — when there really are 3 | Pro |
| **Cart activity** | How many people added this recently | Pro |

Exact machine names, surfaces and page scopes:
[reference/notification-types](../reference/notification-types.generated.md).

heading_path: Notifications (recipes) beyond the cart › Real data only
summary: Recipes are merchant-configured toasts that fire on page views rather than on the shopper's own cart — countdown, announcement, low stock and cart activity.
text:
This is the rule the app will not bend. A countdown counts to a date **you** set.
Low stock reads **live** inventory and stays silent when stock is healthy. Cart
activity counts genuine add-to-cart events the app recorded server-side.

Consequence you should expect: **on a quiet store, the social-proof recipes show
nothing.** That is not a bug — the app would rather say nothing than invent a
number. See [insights-and-roi](insights-and-roi) for the same principle applied
to metrics.

heading_path: Notifications (recipes) beyond the cart › Everything passes the frequency rules
summary: Recipes are merchant-configured toasts that fire on page views rather than on the shopper's own cart — countdown, announcement, low stock and cart activity.
text:
No recipe can flood a shopper. Every one of them is checked against the caps,
cooldowns and quiet mode described in
[anti-spam-and-frequency](anti-spam-and-frequency) before it renders — including
your own announcement.

heading_path: Notifications (recipes) beyond the cart › Where they show
summary: Recipes are merchant-configured toasts that fire on page views rather than on the shopper's own cart — countdown, announcement, low stock and cart activity.
text:
Each recipe can be limited to certain pages, and the whole app can be limited by
[targeting](targeting) (Pro) and by URL exclusions.

Related: [cart-toasts](cart-toasts), [anti-spam-and-frequency](anti-spam-and-frequency),
[plans-free-vs-pro](plans-free-vs-pro).

heading_path: Performance and theme compatibility › Weight on the storefront
summary: How much Won Toasts weighs on the storefront, why it cannot clash with your theme's CSS, and which themes it is tested against.
text:
The storefront script is a single asset served by Shopify's CDN through a theme
app extension, held under a hard **11 kB gzipped** budget that is enforced by a
test in the release gate — the build fails rather than quietly getting heavier.
It does not block rendering and does not reserve layout space, so it cannot cause
layout shift.

There is no `<script>` tag injected into your theme, no ScriptTag API, and no
theme file is modified.

heading_path: Performance and theme compatibility › Why it can't clash with your theme
section: Why it can't clash with your theme
summary: How much Won Toasts weighs on the storefront, why it cannot clash with your theme's CSS, and which themes it is tested against.
text:
Toasts render inside a **Shadow DOM** web component. Your theme's CSS cannot
reach into it and its CSS cannot leak out — which is why a toast looks the same
on a heavily customized theme as on a stock one.

The consequence worth knowing: if you write [custom CSS](../tasks/add-custom-css)
(Pro), it is applied *inside* that shadow root against the app's own class names,
not against your theme's selectors.

heading_path: Performance and theme compatibility › Themes it is tested on
summary: How much Won Toasts weighs on the storefront, why it cannot clash with your theme's CSS, and which themes it is tested against.
text:
Dawn and Horizon, in both desktop and mobile viewports, as part of the release
gate. Other Online Store 2.0 themes work the same way — the app only needs the
app embed, not specific theme markup.

heading_path: Performance and theme compatibility › What it reads from the storefront
section: What it reads from the storefront
summary: How much Won Toasts weighs on the storefront, why it cannot clash with your theme's CSS, and which themes it is tested against.
text:
The shopper's cart, via Shopify's own cart endpoints, to detect what changed.
It writes to the cart exactly once, and only when a shopper clicks **Undo** on a
removed item. It never changes prices, quantities or discounts on its own.

Related: [what-is-won-toasts](what-is-won-toasts), [accessibility](accessibility).

heading_path: Free vs Pro — the idea
summary: The philosophy behind Free vs Pro — Pro gates scope and reach, never basic quality or usability.
text:
Won Toasts has two plans: **Free** and **Pro** ($5/month). The guiding rule is:

> **Pro gates _scope_, never _quality_.**

That means the Free plan is genuinely usable — it keeps **all** cart events,
Undo, every supported language, the live preview, accessibility, and a clean
default look. Free is not a crippled demo.

Pro adds *more* customization and reach: the design studio, custom CSS, advanced
grouping, targeting, unlimited milestones, analytics, experiments, and it removes
the "Powered by Won" badge.

For the **exact, always-current** list of what each plan includes (limits and
feature keys), see the generated
[reference/plan-limits](../reference/plan-limits.generated.md) — that page is
generated from code so it never drifts.

Related: [appearance-and-branding](appearance-and-branding), [targeting](targeting),
[milestones](milestones).

heading_path: What data Won Toasts stores › Permissions it asks for
summary: Which permissions Won Toasts asks for, what it stores, what it deliberately does not store, and what happens on uninstall.
text:
At install the app requests a deliberately small set of scopes: read access to
themes, locales and shipping. That is what it needs to place the app embed, offer
your store's languages, and reason about shipping thresholds.

It does **not** request order or customer scopes. Order-driven features
(order summary, recent sales) stay switched off until Shopify's **Protected
customer data** approval is granted — see
[reference/notification-types](../reference/notification-types.generated.md).

heading_path: What data Won Toasts stores › What it stores
summary: Which permissions Won Toasts asks for, what it stores, what it deliberately does not store, and what happens on uninstall.
text:
- Your **configuration** — appearance, behaviour, messages, milestones, targeting.
- A **version history** of that configuration, so a change can be rolled back.
- **Aggregate counters** for Insights — per day, per toast type.

heading_path: What data Won Toasts stores › What it does not store
summary: Which permissions Won Toasts asks for, what it stores, what it deliberately does not store, and what happens on uninstall.
text:
No shopper names, emails, addresses or IP addresses. Analytics events pass
through a scrubbing gate that keeps only a fixed whitelist of typed fields and
drops everything else, including anything unexpected an integration might attach.

On the storefront, per-shopper state (which milestone was already celebrated,
which toast was dismissed, session counters) lives in the browser's
`sessionStorage` and disappears when the session ends. It is never sent to the app.

heading_path: What data Won Toasts stores › Uninstall and deletion requests
summary: Which permissions Won Toasts asks for, what it stores, what it deliberately does not store, and what happens on uninstall.
text:
Uninstalling triggers a webhook that deletes the store's data. The app also
implements Shopify's mandatory privacy webhooks — customer data request, customer
redaction and shop redaction — and answers them for the data it holds.

Related: [insights-and-roi](insights-and-roi).

heading_path: Targeting (where toasts show)
summary: Targeting (a Pro feature) restricts toasts to specific page types, devices, or customer states.
text:
**Targeting is a Pro feature.** By default toasts show everywhere; targeting lets
you narrow that.

heading_path: Targeting (where toasts show) › What you can target
summary: Targeting (a Pro feature) restricts toasts to specific page types, devices, or customer states.
text:
- **Page type** — product, collection, cart, home, search, other. Empty = all pages.
- **Device** — both, mobile only, or desktop only.
- **Customer state** — both, guests only, or logged-in only.

Exact accepted values: [reference/config-options](../reference/config-options.generated.md).

heading_path: Targeting (where toasts show) › How it's enforced
summary: Targeting (a Pro feature) restricts toasts to specific page types, devices, or customer states.
text:
Targeting is applied **server-side** (in the app-proxy) before the storefront ever
receives the config, so on the Free plan targeting is simply reset to "show
everywhere" — the storefront just renders whatever it's given.

heading_path: Targeting (where toasts show) › One caveat about customer state
summary: Targeting (a Pro feature) restricts toasts to specific page types, devices, or customer states.
text:
The storefront can reliably tell the **page type** and **device**, but it cannot
always tell whether the shopper is logged in. When it can't, the customer-state
filter is ignored (toasts show) rather than guessing wrong.

Related: [plans-free-vs-pro](plans-free-vs-pro), task:
[configure-targeting](../tasks/configure-targeting.md).

heading_path: What Won Toasts does
summary: Won Toasts shows lightweight cart notifications ("toasts") and progress toward shipping/gift milestones in your storefront.
text:
Won Toasts adds **lightweight cart notifications** ("toasts") to your storefront.
When a shopper adds, removes, or changes items, a small message appears — with the
product image, name, and quantity change — and can nudge them toward rewards like
**free shipping** or a **free gift**. It also shows toasts you configure yourself:
a countdown, an announcement, or honest urgency from live inventory and real
cart activity.

heading_path: What Won Toasts does › What a shopper sees
summary: Won Toasts shows lightweight cart notifications ("toasts") and progress toward shipping/gift milestones in your storefront.
text:
- A toast slides in when the cart changes (add / remove / increase / decrease).
- Removed items show an **Undo** action that re-adds them.
- Progress messages appear as the cart approaches a milestone ("You're $12 away
  from free shipping") and celebrate when it's reached.

heading_path: What Won Toasts does › What a merchant controls (in the app admin)
section: What a merchant controls (in the app admin)
summary: Won Toasts shows lightweight cart notifications ("toasts") and progress toward shipping/gift milestones in your storefront.
text:
Everything is configuration — there are no code changes. The admin has:

- **Home** — turn the app on, enable the app embed, see reach at a glance.
- **Toasts** — which recipes are on: cart toasts, milestones, countdown,
  announcement, and the Pro urgency recipes.
- **Design** — look (colours, shape, motion), placement, timing, anti-spam,
  custom CSS.
- **Markets** — languages, translations, per-currency thresholds.
- **Targeting** — URL exclusions on every plan; page / device / customer
  narrowing on Pro.
- **Insights** *(Pro)* — impressions, interactions, holdout-proven ROI.
- **Plan** — Free vs Pro, upgrade and cancel.

heading_path: What Won Toasts does › Where it runs
summary: Won Toasts shows lightweight cart notifications ("toasts") and progress toward shipping/gift milestones in your storefront.
text:
Toasts render on the storefront inside a **Shadow DOM** web component, isolated
from the theme's CSS so they look consistent across themes (tested on Dawn and
Horizon). The app **announces** progress — it never changes prices or grants the
reward itself; your Shopify discounts/shipping rules do that.

heading_path: What Won Toasts does › Key principle
summary: Won Toasts shows lightweight cart notifications ("toasts") and progress toward shipping/gift milestones in your storefront.
text:
Won Toasts **notifies, it does not grant.** A "free shipping" toast reflects your
existing Shopify shipping settings; the app only shows progress toward them.

Related: [cart-toasts](cart-toasts), [milestones](milestones),
[notifications-and-recipes](notifications-and-recipes),
[plans-free-vs-pro](plans-free-vs-pro),
[turn-on-won-toasts](../tasks/turn-on-won-toasts).

doc_title: Why a toast did or didn't show
heading_path: Why a toast did or didn't show
summary: The exact order of checks a toast passes before it renders, so you can tell which one silenced it.
text:
Most "it's broken" reports are a toast that was **decided against**, not one that
failed. The checks run in a fixed order, and the first one that says no wins.

doc_title: Why a toast did or didn't show
heading_path: Why a toast did or didn't show › The order
summary: The exact order of checks a toast passes before it renders, so you can tell which one silenced it.
text:
1. **Is the app on?** The toggle on the app **Home** page.
2. **Is the app embed enabled?** In the theme editor. Without it nothing loads at
   all — no script, no toast. See [turn-on-won-toasts](../tasks/turn-on-won-toasts).
3. **Is this page excluded?** A URL in *Run everywhere, except…* suppresses the
   app completely on that page.
4. **Does targeting match?** *(Pro)* Page type, device and customer state must all
   match, or the app stays inactive for this visitor.
5. **Quiet mode?** If on, everything is muted until it expires.
6. **Is the recipe on?** Cart toasts, countdown, announcement and the Pro recipes
   each have their own switch.
7. **Merging.** Several changes arriving together become one toast — so a "missing"
   toast is often folded into the one you did see, with a `+N`.
8. **Rate limit and caps.** Per-minute rate limit, per-session cap, per-rule
   cooldown, and "stays hidden after the shopper dismissed it".
9. **Does the data support it?** Low stock stays silent above your threshold, cart
   activity stays silent without real activity, a countdown stops after its end
   date. See [notifications-and-recipes](notifications-and-recipes).
10. **Render.** Only now does the shopper see anything.

doc_title: Why a toast did or didn't show
heading_path: Why a toast did or didn't show › Reading it in the other direction
section: Reading it in the other direction
summary: The exact order of checks a toast passes before it renders, so you can tell which one silenced it.
text:
- **Nothing at all on any page** → steps 1–3.
- **Nothing for some visitors only** → step 4 (targeting) or a holdout group.
- **Fewer toasts than expected** → steps 5–8, in that order.
- **One toast instead of three** → step 7. This is working as intended.
- **A social-proof recipe never speaks** → step 9. Also intended.

doc_title: Why a toast did or didn't show
heading_path: Why a toast did or didn't show › What is never the cause
summary: The exact order of checks a toast passes before it renders, so you can tell which one silenced it.
text:
The app does not silently drop a toast because of an error in your settings. An
invalid value falls back to its default and the rest keeps working — a broken
number can make a toast *different*, never randomly absent.

Related: [anti-spam-and-frequency](anti-spam-and-frequency),
[troubleshooting](../support/troubleshooting.md).

heading_path: Notification (recipe) types
summary: Every notification type a merchant can turn on, which plan it needs, where it can render and which page scopes it accepts.
text:
Cart toasts react to the shopper's own cart. **Notifications** (shown in the
admin as recipes on the **Toasts** page) are merchant-configured rules that can
fire on a page view instead. Every one of them is bound by the frequency rules on
the **Design → Anti-spam** section, and by the plan below.

Locked principle: **real data only.** A countdown counts to a date you set, low
stock reads live inventory, cart activity counts genuine server-side add-to-cart
events. The app never invents a number, and stays silent instead of guessing on a
quiet store.

heading_path: Notification (recipe) types › Order-data types are off at launch
section: Order-data types are off at launch
summary: Every notification type a merchant can turn on, which plan it needs, where it can render and which page scopes it accepts.
text:
`order.summary` and `order.created` read order data, which needs Shopify's
**Protected customer data** approval. Until that is granted the app ships without
them: the `orders/create` webhook stays off and neither type can fire. Cart
activity does **not** need it — it counts add-to-cart events the app records
itself.

DOM) and show nothing when the underlying count is too low to be honest:

- `order.summary`

heading_path: Frequently asked questions
summary: Short answers to the questions asked most often before and just after installing Won Toasts.
text:
**Does it change my theme files?**
No. It runs as a theme app extension you enable in the theme editor. Nothing is
written into your theme, and uninstalling leaves no leftovers.

**Will it slow my store down?**
The storefront script is held under an 11 kB gzipped budget enforced by a build
test, does not block rendering and causes no layout shift. See
[performance-and-compatibility](../concepts/performance-and-compatibility).

**Will it clash with my theme's styling?**
It cannot — toasts render inside a Shadow DOM, isolated in both directions.

**Does a "free shipping" toast actually make shipping free?**
No. The app announces progress toward a threshold you configure; the actual free
shipping comes from your Shopify shipping rate. Set both to the same number.

**Can I use it on a brand-new store with no orders?**
Yes. Cart toasts, countdown and announcement need no history. The social-proof
recipes stay silent until there is real activity — deliberately.

**Do you show fake numbers to create urgency?**
No. Low stock reads live inventory, cart activity counts genuine server-side
events, countdowns count to a date you set. When the data isn't there, the app
shows nothing.

**What does it cost?**
There is a free plan. Pro is a recurring subscription billed by Shopify — see
[upgrade-to-pro](../tasks/upgrade-to-pro) and
[reference/plan-limits](../reference/plan-limits.generated.md).

heading_path: Frequently asked questions
summary: Short answers to the questions asked most often before and just after installing Won Toasts.
text:
**What data do you collect about my shoppers?**
No names, emails, addresses or IPs. Only aggregate counts per toast type, and
your own configuration. See [privacy-and-data](../concepts/privacy-and-data).

**Is it accessible?**
Screen-reader announcements, reduced-motion support, dark-mode support and touch
targets are on every plan. See [accessibility](../concepts/accessibility).

**Which languages does it support?**
Whichever your store publishes, plus any BCP-47 code you add — with correct plural
forms. See [translate-toast-messages](../tasks/translate-toast-messages).

**Can I turn it off on checkout?**
Yes, with a URL exclusion, on any plan. See
[exclude-pages-and-urls](../tasks/exclude-pages-and-urls).

heading_path: Troubleshooting toasts › Toasts don't appear at all
summary: Common Won Toasts issues and their causes — toasts not showing, free shipping not applying, gift toasts, branding.
text:
1. **Is the app enabled?** Check the toggle on the app **Home** page
   (*Show Won Toasts on the storefront*).
2. **Is the app embed turned on?** In the Shopify **theme editor → App embeds**,
   enable the Won Toasts embed and save. Without it, nothing renders on the
   storefront.
3. **URL exclusions:** the **Targeting** page has *Run everywhere, except…*. A
   path listed there (e.g. `/checkout*`) renders nothing at all.
4. **Targeting (Pro):** if you narrowed by page/device/customer, the current
   visitor may fall outside it. Clear targeting to test.
5. **Quiet mode:** **Design → Anti-spam → Quiet mode** mutes everything until it
   expires.

heading_path: Troubleshooting toasts › "Free shipping unlocked" but checkout still charges shipping
section: "Free shipping unlocked" but checkout still charges shipping
summary: Common Won Toasts issues and their causes — toasts not showing, free shipping not applying, gift toasts, branding.
text:
The app **announces** the milestone; it does not make shipping free. Add a matching
free-shipping rate in **Shopify Settings → Shipping and delivery** at the same
subtotal threshold. See [set-up-free-shipping-milestone](../tasks/set-up-free-shipping-milestone.md).

heading_path: Troubleshooting toasts › A free gift was added but no toast (or the wrong toast) showed
section: A free gift was added but no toast (or the wrong toast) showed
summary: Common Won Toasts issues and their causes — toasts not showing, free shipping not applying, gift toasts, branding.
text:
Gift lines (added by a gift/gift-ladder mechanism, marked `_gift_progress`) are
deliberately **not** treated as normal "item added" toasts — they surface as a
**gift milestone** instead. See [milestones](../concepts/milestones.md).

heading_path: Troubleshooting toasts › Too many toasts at once
summary: Common Won Toasts issues and their causes — toasts not showing, free shipping not applying, gift toasts, branding.
text:
Tune **Design → Anti-spam**: merge first (group by, merge window, `+N`), then the
caps (per session, cooldown, hide after dismiss). Step-by-step:
[tune-anti-spam](../tasks/tune-anti-spam.md), background:
[grouping-and-conflicts](../concepts/grouping-and-conflicts.md).

heading_path: Troubleshooting toasts › A toast fired far less often than expected
section: A toast fired far less often than expected
summary: Common Won Toasts issues and their causes — toasts not showing, free shipping not applying, gift toasts, branding.
text:
It was probably governed, not broken. The suppression order is: quiet mode →
per-session cap → cooldown → hidden after the shopper dismissed it. See
[anti-spam-and-frequency](../concepts/anti-spam-and-frequency.md).

heading_path: Troubleshooting toasts › Low stock / cart activity show nothing
section: Low stock / cart activity show nothing
summary: Common Won Toasts issues and their causes — toasts not showing, free shipping not applying, gift toasts, branding.
text:
By design — they only speak when the real number supports it. New or quiet stores
see nothing. See
[show-low-stock-and-cart-activity](../tasks/show-low-stock-and-cart-activity.md).

heading_path: Troubleshooting toasts › A shopper sees the wrong language
section: A shopper sees the wrong language
summary: Common Won Toasts issues and their causes — toasts not showing, free shipping not applying, gift toasts, branding.
text:
Check **Markets**: the language must be in *Your languages* and have a
translation, otherwise the fallback chain lands on your default language. See
[translate-toast-messages](../tasks/translate-toast-messages.md).

heading_path: Troubleshooting toasts › The free-shipping bar shows the wrong amount in another currency
section: The free-shipping bar shows the wrong amount in another currency
summary: Common Won Toasts issues and their causes — toasts not showing, free shipping not applying, gift toasts, branding.
text:
Thresholds are set **per currency**, not converted. Fill the missing one under
**Markets → Currencies** — see
[set-thresholds-per-currency](../tasks/set-thresholds-per-currency.md).

heading_path: Troubleshooting toasts › Pro settings stopped applying
summary: Common Won Toasts issues and their causes — toasts not showing, free shipping not applying, gift toasts, branding.

heading_path: Troubleshooting toasts › My custom CSS does nothing
summary: Common Won Toasts issues and their causes — toasts not showing, free shipping not applying, gift toasts, branding.
text:
It is injected **inside** the Shadow DOM, so theme selectors do not resolve there.
See [add-custom-css](../tasks/add-custom-css.md).

heading_path: Troubleshooting toasts › "Powered by Won" badge
summary: Common Won Toasts issues and their causes — toasts not showing, free shipping not applying, gift toasts, branding.
text:
The badge shows on the **Free** plan. Removing it is a Pro feature. See
[reference/plan-limits](../reference/plan-limits.generated.md).

heading_path: Troubleshooting toasts › A setting didn't take effect
summary: Common Won Toasts issues and their causes — toasts not showing, free shipping not applying, gift toasts, branding.
text:
Invalid values are ignored and fall back to the default (this is intentional, to
avoid breaking the storefront). Re-check the value against
[reference/config-options](../reference/config-options.generated.md) and save again.

heading_path: Add custom CSS (Pro)
summary: Style toasts beyond the design studio with your own CSS, and what to know about the shadow root it runs in.
text: **Design → Custom CSS**. Up to 4000 characters.

heading_path: Add custom CSS (Pro) › It runs inside the shadow root
section: It runs inside the shadow root
summary: Style toasts beyond the design studio with your own CSS, and what to know about the shadow root it runs in.
text:
Toasts live in a Shadow DOM, so your CSS is injected *inside* that shadow root.
Two consequences:

- Your **theme's** selectors and variables are not visible in there. Copying a
  rule from your theme stylesheet will usually do nothing.
- Your rules cannot leak out and break the rest of the page — which is why this
  feature can be offered at all.

Target the app's own elements and the CSS custom properties the design studio
sets, rather than theme class names.

heading_path: Add custom CSS (Pro) › Try the design studio first
summary: Style toasts beyond the design studio with your own CSS, and what to know about the shadow root it runs in.
text:
Colours, corner radius, width, shadow, density, animation, per-event accent, icon
style and font are all fields in **Design** — no CSS needed, and they stay
consistent with the live preview. Reach for custom CSS only for what those fields
cannot express.

heading_path: Add custom CSS (Pro) › Preview it
summary: Style toasts beyond the design studio with your own CSS, and what to know about the shadow root it runs in.
text:
The live preview on the Design page renders through the same component as the
storefront, so what you see there is what a shopper gets.

heading_path: Add custom CSS (Pro) › If it stops applying
summary: Style toasts beyond the design studio with your own CSS, and what to know about the shadow root it runs in.
text:
Custom CSS is Pro. On Free it is kept but not applied — see
[upgrade-to-pro](upgrade-to-pro).

Related: [appearance-and-branding](../concepts/appearance-and-branding),
[performance-and-compatibility](../concepts/performance-and-compatibility).

heading_path: Configure targeting
summary: How to restrict where toasts appear by page, device, or customer state (Pro).
text:
**Targeting is a Pro feature.** On Free, toasts show everywhere and the targeting
settings are ignored.

heading_path: Configure targeting › Steps (Pro)
summary: How to restrict where toasts appear by page, device, or customer state (Pro).
text:
1. Open the **Targeting** admin page.
2. Pick **page types** to allow (leave empty to show on all pages).
3. Choose a **device** filter (both / mobile / desktop).
4. Choose a **customer state** filter (both / guests / logged-in).
5. Save.

Accepted values: [reference/config-options](../reference/config-options.generated.md).

heading_path: Configure targeting › Notes
summary: How to restrict where toasts appear by page, device, or customer state (Pro).
text:
- Targeting is enforced server-side, so it applies before toasts reach the browser.
- **Customer state** is only applied when the storefront can tell whether the
  shopper is logged in; when it can't, toasts show rather than guessing.

Related: [targeting](../concepts/targeting.md).

heading_path: Show your own announcement
summary: Put your own message on the storefront without touching the theme, optionally split-tested across variants.
text:
Use this for a sale, a shipping cutoff, a holiday note — anything you would
otherwise hard-code into the theme.

1. Go to **Toasts** → **Announcement**.
2. Turn on **Show an announcement**.
3. Write the **Message**. Example: *Free gift on orders over 1000 Kč this week!*
4. Save.

heading_path: Show your own announcement › Translate it
summary: Put your own message on the storefront without touching the theme, optionally split-tested across variants.
text:
An announcement carries a message per language. Fill the other languages under
**Markets → Translations**; a shopper on a language you left blank falls back to
your default language rather than seeing nothing. See
[translate-toast-messages](translate-toast-messages).

heading_path: Show your own announcement › Split-test it (optional)
summary: Put your own message on the storefront without touching the theme, optionally split-tested across variants.
text:
Put several lines into **A/B variants (one per line)** and shoppers are split
evenly between them. The assignment is stable per shopper, so nobody watches the
message change mid-visit. Results appear under **Insights** (Pro) — see
[insights-and-roi](../concepts/insights-and-roi).

heading_path: Show your own announcement › It still obeys the caps
summary: Put your own message on the storefront without touching the theme, optionally split-tested across variants.
text:
An announcement is governed like every other recipe: session cap, cooldown, and
"stays hidden after a shopper dismisses it". If yours shows less often than you
expect, check **Design → Anti-spam** — see [tune-anti-spam](tune-anti-spam).

heading_path: Customize toast appearance
summary: How to change toast colors, animation and layout in the design studio (Pro), with a live preview.
text:
**Design studio is a Pro feature.** On Free, toasts use the neutral default look
(light/dark/system), which cannot be restyled but is fully usable.

heading_path: Customize toast appearance › Steps (Pro)
summary: How to change toast colors, animation and layout in the design studio (Pro), with a live preview.
text:
1. Open the **Appearance** admin page.
2. Choose a **theme mode** (system / light / dark / custom). Custom unlocks colors.
3. Adjust radius, width, shadow, density, animation, icon set.
4. Optionally set a **per-event accent** color (e.g. green for "added").
5. Use the **live preview** (and Scenario Lab) to check the result — it renders
   with the same engine as the storefront.
6. Save.

Accepted values for every option:
[reference/config-options](../reference/config-options.generated.md).

heading_path: Customize toast appearance › Notes
summary: How to change toast colors, animation and layout in the design studio (Pro), with a live preview.
text:
- Changes are safe: invalid values are ignored and fall back to the default.
- The default look already adapts to the shopper's light/dark preference and to
  reduced-motion — you don't have to configure that.

Related: [appearance-and-branding](../concepts/appearance-and-branding.md).

doc_title: Turn toasts off on specific pages
heading_path: Turn toasts off on specific pages
summary: Keep toasts off checkout, legal pages or a specific campaign landing page using URL exclusions.
text:
Exclusions are on the **Targeting** page under **Run everywhere, except…** — and
unlike targeting itself, they are available on every plan.

1. Go to **Targeting**.
2. Under **Specific URLs**, list the paths to stay off, one per line:

   ```
   /checkout*
   /pages/legal
   ```

3. `*` matches the rest of the path, so `/checkout*` covers every checkout step.
4. Save.

doc_title: Turn toasts off on specific pages
heading_path: Turn toasts off on specific pages › Exclusion beats everything else
summary: Keep toasts off checkout, legal pages or a specific campaign landing page using URL exclusions.
text:
If a page is excluded, nothing renders there — not cart toasts, not an
announcement, not a countdown. It is the reliable way to guarantee a clean page.

doc_title: Turn toasts off on specific pages
heading_path: Turn toasts off on specific pages › Narrowing instead of excluding (Pro)
summary: Keep toasts off checkout, legal pages or a specific campaign landing page using URL exclusions.
text:
To *choose* where toasts run rather than carve pages out, use **Narrow it down** —
page type, **Devices**, **Customers**. That part is Pro. See
[configure-targeting](configure-targeting).

Related: [targeting](../concepts/targeting).

heading_path: Set free-shipping thresholds per currency
summary: Give each presentment currency its own free-shipping threshold so the progress bar always matches your real Shopify shipping rate.
text:
1. Turn the free-shipping milestone on first — **Toasts** → **Cart toasts** →
   **Free-shipping threshold**. See
   [set-up-free-shipping-milestone](set-up-free-shipping-milestone).
2. Go to **Markets** → **Currencies**.
3. For each **Currency**, enter its **Threshold** — the amount in that currency,
   not a converted number.
4. Save.

heading_path: Set free-shipping thresholds per currency › Why per currency and not converted
section: Why per currency and not converted
summary: Give each presentment currency its own free-shipping threshold so the progress bar always matches your real Shopify shipping rate.
text:
An automatically converted threshold drifts with the exchange rate, so the bar the
shopper sees stops matching the free-shipping rate you set in **Shopify Settings →
Shipping and delivery**. Entering the number per currency keeps the promise and
the actual rate aligned.

Set each threshold to the same number as the matching Shopify shipping rate for
that market.

heading_path: Set free-shipping thresholds per currency › Plan limits
summary: Give each presentment currency its own free-shipping threshold so the progress bar always matches your real Shopify shipping rate.
text:
Free keeps a limited number of per-currency thresholds. When you exceed it, the
ones kept are chosen alphabetically by ISO code — deterministically, so a
shopper's progress bar never changes between page loads. Exact numbers in
[reference/plan-limits](../reference/plan-limits.generated.md).

Related: [markets-languages-currencies](../concepts/markets-languages-currencies),
[milestones](../concepts/milestones).

heading_path: Set up a countdown timer
summary: Put a real deadline on the storefront — either a fixed end date or an evergreen timer that restarts per visitor.
text:
1. Go to **Toasts** → **Countdown timer**.
2. Turn on **Show a countdown**.
3. Choose what it counts to:
   - **Fixed end date** — set **End date**. Everyone sees the same deadline.
   - **Evergreen** — set **Restart for each visitor after**. Each visitor gets
     their own window from their first visit.
4. Save.

heading_path: Set up a countdown timer › What it will not do
summary: Put a real deadline on the storefront — either a fixed end date or an evergreen timer that restarts per visitor.
text:
The countdown only ever counts to a date you set. It cannot generate a fake
deadline, and when a fixed end date passes it stops showing rather than looping.

If you use the evergreen mode, be honest about what the deadline means — the app
enforces the mechanics, not your copy.

heading_path: Set up a countdown timer › Pair it with a real discount
section: Pair it with a real discount
summary: Put a real deadline on the storefront — either a fixed end date or an evergreen timer that restarts per visitor.
text:
Like every toast, this **announces**; it does not create the offer. Set the actual
discount in Shopify so the deadline the shopper sees and the discount that applies
end at the same moment.

Related: [notifications-and-recipes](../concepts/notifications-and-recipes).

heading_path: Set up a free-shipping milestone
summary: How to configure a free-shipping progress milestone, and the Shopify setting that actually makes shipping free.
text:
Won Toasts shows the shopper how close they are to free shipping and celebrates
when they cross the threshold.

heading_path: Set up a free-shipping milestone › Steps
summary: How to configure a free-shipping progress milestone, and the Shopify setting that actually makes shipping free.
text:
1. In the app admin, open **Events & messages**.
2. Add a **free shipping** milestone and set the **subtotal threshold** (the cart
   amount at which shipping becomes free).
3. Optionally edit the progress and celebration message templates (per language).
4. Save.

Free plans can have up to a limited number of active milestones — see
[reference/plan-limits](../reference/plan-limits.generated.md).

heading_path: Set up a free-shipping milestone › Important: this announces, it does not grant
section: Important: this announces, it does not grant
summary: How to configure a free-shipping progress milestone, and the Shopify setting that actually makes shipping free.
text:
The milestone **only shows progress**. Shipping actually becomes free because of
your **Shopify shipping settings**, not the app. Set a matching free-shipping rate
in **Shopify Settings → Shipping and delivery** (a free rate above the same
subtotal). Keep the two thresholds equal.

If a toast says "free shipping unlocked" but checkout still charges shipping, the
Shopify shipping rate is the thing to fix — the app is reporting progress toward a
threshold you set, it never changes the shipping price.

Related: [milestones](../concepts/milestones.md).

doc_title: Show low stock and cart activity (Pro)
heading_path: Show low stock and cart activity (Pro)
summary: Turn on the two honest urgency recipes — live inventory and server-counted add-to-cart activity — and understand when they stay silent.
text:
Both recipes are Pro. Both read real data, and both show **nothing** when the real
data does not support a claim.

doc_title: Show low stock and cart activity (Pro)
heading_path: Show low stock and cart activity (Pro) › Low-stock urgency
summary: Turn on the two honest urgency recipes — live inventory and server-counted add-to-cart activity — and understand when they stay silent.
text:
1. **Toasts** → **Low-stock urgency** → turn on **Show low-stock nudges**.
2. Set **Show when inventory is below** — the threshold at which a product counts
   as scarce.
3. Save.

It reads your live inventory. Above the threshold, the shopper sees nothing. There
is no way to make it say "only 3 left" when there are 300 — that is the point.

doc_title: Show low stock and cart activity (Pro)
heading_path: Show low stock and cart activity (Pro) › Cart activity
summary: Turn on the two honest urgency recipes — live inventory and server-counted add-to-cart activity — and understand when they stay silent.
text:
1. **Toasts** → **Cart activity** → turn on **Show cart activity**.
2. Set **Look back over** — how many hours of activity to count (24 = one day).
3. Save.

It counts genuine add-to-cart events the app recorded server-side. It does **not**
need order access or Shopify's protected customer data approval.

doc_title: Show low stock and cart activity (Pro)
heading_path: Show low stock and cart activity (Pro) › Why it might show nothing
summary: Turn on the two honest urgency recipes — live inventory and server-counted add-to-cart activity — and understand when they stay silent.
text:
Because the number is real. A new or quiet store has no activity to report, and
the app stays silent instead of inventing one. If you need something visible on
day one, use [countdown](set-up-a-countdown) or
[announcement](create-an-announcement) — both work with no history.

Related: [notifications-and-recipes](../concepts/notifications-and-recipes),
[insights-and-roi](../concepts/insights-and-roi).

heading_path: Translate toast messages
summary: Add languages, translate every message type, and set the fallback language shoppers get when a translation is missing.
text: Everything lives on the **Markets** page.

heading_path: Translate toast messages › 1. Pick your languages
summary: Add languages, translate every message type, and set the fallback language shoppers get when a translation is missing.
text:
**Your languages** lists the languages your Shopify store publishes. Add anything
extra as BCP-47 codes in **Extra language codes** (`pt-pt, sv, da`).

Set **Default (fallback) language** — this is what a shopper gets when their own
language has no translation.

Free plans carry fewer languages than Pro; the limits are in
[reference/plan-limits](../reference/plan-limits.generated.md).

heading_path: Translate toast messages › 2. Translate
summary: Add languages, translate every message type, and set the fallback language shoppers get when a translation is missing.
text:
Under **Translations**, fill the message for each toast type in each language.
Placeholders (product name, quantity, amount remaining) are filled in by the app
and must stay in the text.

Plural forms are handled for you, including languages with more than two plural
categories such as Czech and Slovak — write the template, not the branching.

heading_path: Translate toast messages › 3. Check the fallback chain
summary: Add languages, translate every message type, and set the fallback language shoppers get when a translation is missing.
text:
A shopper on `pt-BR` gets: `pt-BR` → `pt` → your default language → English.
A missing translation is never an empty toast.

Related: [markets-languages-currencies](../concepts/markets-languages-currencies).

heading_path: Show fewer toasts (anti-spam tuning)
summary: The order to work through when toasts feel too frequent — merge first, then caps, then quiet mode.
text:
All of it lives under **Design → Anti-spam**. Work top-down; each layer is
cheaper than the one below it.

heading_path: Show fewer toasts (anti-spam tuning) › 1. Merge first
summary: The order to work through when toasts feel too frequent — merge first, then caps, then quiet mode.
text:
- **Group by** — widen it (e.g. group by product rather than variant) and several
  changes become one toast.
- **Merge changes within** — a longer window catches more of a burst.
- **Merge quantity changes into one "+N"** — on.

Merging keeps the information and removes the stack, so try it before capping.

heading_path: Show fewer toasts (anti-spam tuning) › 2. Then cap
summary: The order to work through when toasts feel too frequent — merge first, then caps, then quiet mode.
text:
- **Max toasts per session** — the ceiling per visit.
- **Wait between repeats** — a cooldown before the same toast may return.
- **Hide a dismissed toast for** — respect a shopper who closed it.
- **Advanced caps** *(Pro)* — max per minute, and ignoring duplicates within a window.

On Free the per-session cap is a fixed number you cannot raise; Pro lets you set
it, including `0` for unlimited. See
[reference/plan-limits](../reference/plan-limits.generated.md).

heading_path: Show fewer toasts (anti-spam tuning) › 3. Quiet mode when you need silence
section: 3. Quiet mode when you need silence
summary: The order to work through when toasts feel too frequent — merge first, then caps, then quiet mode.
text:
**Quiet mode** mutes everything — useful during a theme migration or a campaign
you don't want commented on. Remember to switch it back off.

heading_path: Show fewer toasts (anti-spam tuning) › Also check what's on
summary: The order to work through when toasts feel too frequent — merge first, then caps, then quiet mode.
text:
Fewer toasts sometimes just means fewer recipes. **Toasts** shows every recipe
with its on/off state; turning one off is the bluntest and clearest fix.

Related: [anti-spam-and-frequency](../concepts/anti-spam-and-frequency),
[grouping-and-conflicts](../concepts/grouping-and-conflicts).

heading_path: Turn on Won Toasts (go live)
summary: The two switches that put toasts on your storefront — the app toggle and the theme app embed — and how to verify it worked.
text:
Nothing shows on the storefront until **both** switches are on. The app's home
page walks you through it under **Go live**.

heading_path: Turn on Won Toasts (go live) › 1. Turn on the app
summary: The two switches that put toasts on your storefront — the app toggle and the theme app embed — and how to verify it worked.
text: Home → **Turn on Won Toasts** → enable *Show Won Toasts on the storefront*.

heading_path: Turn on Won Toasts (go live) › 2. Enable the app embed
summary: The two switches that put toasts on your storefront — the app toggle and the theme app embed — and how to verify it worked.
text:
Home → **Enable the app embed**. This deep-links you into the Shopify **theme
editor → App embeds**. Switch Won Toasts on and **Save**.

This step exists because Shopify requires the merchant to allow an app onto the
theme. Won Toasts never edits your theme files.

heading_path: Turn on Won Toasts (go live) › 3. Verify
summary: The two switches that put toasts on your storefront — the app toggle and the theme app embed — and how to verify it worked.
text:
Open your storefront and add something to the cart. You should see a toast.

If nothing appears, the home page shows the live status of both switches — an
embed that was never saved is the single most common cause. See
[troubleshooting](../support/troubleshooting).

heading_path: Turn on Won Toasts (go live) › 4. Then configure
summary: The two switches that put toasts on your storefront — the app toggle and the theme app embed — and how to verify it worked.
text:
- **Toasts** — which recipes are on ([notifications-and-recipes](../concepts/notifications-and-recipes))
- **Design** — look, placement, timing, anti-spam ([customize-appearance](customize-appearance))
- **Markets** — languages and per-currency thresholds ([translate-toast-messages](translate-toast-messages))
- **Targeting** *(Pro)* — where they show ([configure-targeting](configure-targeting))

New store with no traffic yet? Start with the cold-start-safe recipes — cart
toasts, countdown and announcement — which work without any order history.

heading_path: Upgrade to Pro, and cancel › Upgrade
summary: How the Pro subscription is charged through Shopify, how to cancel, and what happens to your settings when you go back to Free.
text:
1. Go to **Plan**.
2. Choose Pro. Shopify's own confirmation page opens.
3. Approve the recurring charge.

Billing is handled by **Shopify**, on the same invoice as your other apps. Won
Toasts never sees a card number. If the subscription cannot be started you get a
plain "Billing error" instead of a half-upgraded account.

heading_path: Upgrade to Pro, and cancel › Cancel
summary: How the Pro subscription is charged through Shopify, how to cancel, and what happens to your settings when you go back to Free.
text:
**Plan** → **Cancel Pro (back to Free)**. You can also cancel from your Shopify
admin's app subscriptions. Cancelling is immediate in the app.

heading_path: Upgrade to Pro, and cancel › What happens to your settings on Free
section: What happens to your settings on Free
summary: How the Pro subscription is charged through Shopify, how to cancel, and what happens to your settings when you go back to Free.
text:
Nothing is deleted. Pro-only settings stop being *applied* — the look falls back
to the default, targeting stops narrowing, extra milestones beyond the Free limit
go inactive, and the "Powered by Won" badge returns. Upgrade again and your
configuration is applied as it was.

This is enforced on the server before the storefront ever sees the config, so a
downgraded store cannot keep serving Pro output.

heading_path: Upgrade to Pro, and cancel › What Pro actually buys
summary: How the Pro subscription is charged through Shopify, how to cancel, and what happens to your settings when you go back to Free.
text:
Scope, never quality: design studio, custom CSS, targeting, advanced anti-spam
caps, unlimited milestones, Insights and experiments, the Pro recipes, and brand
removal. Accessibility, languages, cart toasts and the live preview are on every
plan. Full list:
[reference/plan-limits](../reference/plan-limits.generated.md).

Related: [plans-free-vs-pro](../concepts/plans-free-vs-pro).
